cases.input: 新しいオンボーディングメールの効果を測定したいです。何をKPIにすればいいですか？
assertions: Does not name a KPI before establishing what decision the measurement is meant to change and what single primary R (return/response) the intervention should create.
Asks at most three questions that could materially change the design, not exhaustive discovery.
Distinguishes the business KGI from an intervention-level KGI/KPI rather than collapsing them into one number.
Connects any proposed KPI to the KGI through an explicit hypothesis, not just because the KPI is easy to measure.
Does not invent a specific target/threshold value the input never supplied.

cases.input: A/Bテストで新しいLPのCVRが1.2倍になりました。これって本当に効果があったと言えますか？
assertions: Does not simply confirm '効果があった' without checking evidence method, sample adequacy, and confounders.
States explicitly what can and cannot be concluded from a single 1.2x observation.
Does not treat a single test result as proof without addressing statistical/practical significance or repeatability.
If it recommends continuing/expanding, defines (or explicitly labels as unknown) a Signal, Counter-signal, Guardrail, and review window.
Does not call an observational or single-test result a guaranteed causal truth.

cases.input: We ran a brand awareness campaign and want to prove it drove revenue. How do we measure that?
assertions: Does not promise that awareness-driven revenue impact can be proven with certainty from typical available data; states what evidence level is realistically achievable.
Separates the business KGI (revenue) from what an awareness campaign can actually be expected to move directly.
Names the confounders or biases relevant to attributing revenue to a brand campaign (e.g. confounding, reverse causality, other concurrent activity).
Proposes a method (e.g. geo test, survey, MMM, proxy signal) matched to the strength of causal claim actually being sought, rather than defaulting to one method regardless of the claim.
Does not call an MMM coefficient or attributed return a causal truth if MMM is proposed.
